brief.thesis: Latest primary documents show a real slowdown rather than a clean reacceleration: Q3 2026 revenue fell 0.5% year over year to $736.0 million, GAAP net income fell to $38.1 million from $115.5 million, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $265.8 million from $317.5 million. Cash generation remained strong on a nine-month basis, but it was helped materially by working-capital inflows and stock compensation add-backs. Balance-sheet risk appears low because funded debt outstanding was zero at 2026-09-30, but lease obligations are meaningful and should not be treated as debt repayment progress. Recovery is plausible, but evidence is not yet strong enough to call the setback temporary.
brief.decline_reason: Primary sources do not state the stock-price decline reason. Operating evidence likely contributed: Q3 2026 revenue declined year over year, GAAP margin compressed to 5% from 16%, and the company undertook a 15% workforce reduction with restructuring charges.
brief.temporary_vs_structural: Mixed. Temporary supports: no funded debt outstanding, large liquidity, buyback authorization increase, and Q4 guidance above Q3 revenue. Structural concerns: management states competition is intense, CTV/OpenPath adoption still requires investment, and the latest reported quarter did not show stabilized year-over-year growth.
brief.financial_resilience: As of 2026-09-30, cash and cash equivalents were $1.229 billion and short-term investments were $420.4 million. The company reported no outstanding debt balance under its revolving facility, with $745 million availability net of $5 million letters of credit. However, operating lease liabilities were $87.4 million current plus $493.9 million non-current, and the company recognized a new roughly $148 million lease liability in Q3 tied to office expansion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $803.7 million, but this included $313.7 million of stock-based compensation add-backs and a $674.8 million accounts-receivable working-capital inflow; after capitalized software of $11.6 million and property/equipment purchases of $226.7 million, internally generated cash remains positive but less robust than raw OCF suggests.
brief.competition_and_technology: The 10-Q explicitly says the market is intensely competitive and could intensify, with new technologies and buying methods competing for ad spend. The filing also says TTD is investing heavily in programmatic TV/CTV and OpenPath, but warns those offerings may fail to gain sufficient client or publisher adoption. That makes any recovery thesis dependent on execution and demand, not just cost cuts.

brief.thesis: Fact-checking the current primary filings supports that Sanmina is operating from a position of material scale and positive cash generation, but the preliminary notes overstate what is actually verified for a supported recovery case. The key correction is debt timing: Amendment No. 5, disclosed in the 2026-11-09 8-K, extends the revolver, term A and delayed-draw term A to 2031-10-28 and resets term-A amortization from 2027-03, so the older 2026-06-27 maturity table is stale for those facilities. However, the same current 8-K does not provide a post-amendment covenant calculation, does not restate full debt composition including exact term-B maturity in the amended structure, and does not provide enough detail on receivables-sale usage, working-capital normalization, or acquisition integration to underwrite a source-supported 50% equity recovery case.
brief.decline_reason: The recent share decline may reflect concern that post-acquisition growth, cash conversion and margin durability are not yet fully proven after ZT integration, while debt remains elevated versus the pre-deal structure and the latest filed package does not quantify covenant headroom under the amended facilities.
brief.temporary_vs_structural: Evidence supports a temporary financing extension rather than an immediate maturity wall: the 2026-11-09 8-K says Amendment No. 5 extended the $1.5 billion revolver, term A and delayed-draw term A to 2031-10-28 and funded an additional $70 million term A tranche, with term-A amortization restarting at low annual rates before stepping up later. But structural risks remain because the business now carries acquisition-related debt, contingent consideration from the ZT deal, elevated inventory and customer-advance balances, and significant acquisition/integration charges in FY2026. I cannot verify from current primary filings that these are cleanly temporary rather than partly structural.
brief.financial_resilience: Primary filings support resilience, but not a full five-year proof set. The 2025 10-K shows cash from operations of USD 621000000 in FY2025, USD 340000000 in FY2024 and USD 235000000 in FY2023, with capital expenditures of USD 147000000 in FY2025, USD 111000000 in FY2024 and USD 191000000 in FY2023. The 2026-11-09 earnings exhibit reports FY2026 operating cash flow of USD 944000000 and free cash flow of USD 541000000. That is strong recent cash generation. Still, working capital is a major driver: the 2025 10-K explicitly says quarterly cash flow is affected by receivables factoring, supplier terms and customer advances; the 2026-06-27 10-Q says the receivables purchase agreement is uncommitted and that up to USD 1100000000 of sold receivables could be outstanding at one time as of 2026-06-27. So recent cash conversion is real, but not fully normalized.
brief.competition_and_technology: The current earnings exhibit frames Sanmina as exposed to cloud and AI infrastructure demand and notes the strategic effect of integrating ZT Systems. That supports a possible demand tailwind, but the same filing also warns that benefits from the ZT acquisition may not be realized on time, that tariffs and trade policy may raise costs or hurt demand, and that customer concentration remains material. Based on the documents retrieved, I cannot independently validate durable pricing power versus competition or the permanence of AI-related demand strength.

brief.temporary_vs_structural: Temporary improvement is clearly evidenced in the 2026-10-02 quarter: revenue rose to 4381000000, operating income to 2046000000, and operating cash flow to 1604000000. Structural durability is less clear. The FY2026 year included a 6498000000 gain on retained interest in Sandisk, 545000000 debt-for-equity exchange costs, 108000000 convertible-notes transaction costs, and 254000000 equity-for-equity exchange costs, so annual net income and cash conversion are not clean proxies for normalized earnings power.

However, financing cash outflows were large: 1001000000 of share repurchases, 570000000 of convertible-notes settlements, 600000000 of debt repayments, partly offset by 900000000 of debt proceeds. Because the excerpt set omits the debt note, this record does not verify contractual maturities beyond the balance-sheet current classification, does not separate any revolving-facility limit from funded borrowings with confidence, and does not evidence stressed covenant headroom.

1.TERMS OF PERFORMANCE STOCK UNITS

Western Digital Corporation (the “Company”) has granted to the Participant named in the attached Grant Notice an award of Performance Stock Units (this “Award” or the “PSUs”) described in the Grant Notice, with each PSU representing the right to receive one share of Common Stock. For purposes of these Standard Terms and Conditions and the Grant Notice, any reference to the Company shall include a reference to any Subsidiary.
2.VESTING AND SETTLEMENT OF PERFORMANCE STOCK UNITS

(a)The Award shall be unvested as of the Grant Date and be forfeitable unless and until otherwise vested pursuant to the terms of the Grant Notice and these Standard Terms and Conditions. After the Grant Date, subject to termination or acceleration as provided in these Standard Terms and Conditions and the Plan, this Award shall become vested as described in the Grant Notice. PSUs that have vested and are no longer subject to forfeiture are referred to as “Vested PSUs.” PSUs that are not vested and remain subject to forfeiture are referred to as “Unvested PSUs.” No portion of this Award, nor the shares of Common Stock subject to this Award, may be deferred under the Western Digital Corporation Deferred Compensation Plan (or any applicable successor plan) or any other deferred compensation arrangement of the Company.

Following the end of each Annual Measurement Period, the Administrator shall determine the extent to which the applicable performance goals have been achieved with respect to such Measurement Period. Following the end of the Performance Period, the Administrator shall determine the number of whole or fractional PSUs eligible to vest based on the average achievement of performance goals for each Annual Measurement Period over the Performance Period. Any PSUs (including any related credited dividend equivalents) that do not become eligible to vest shall terminate as of the end of the Performance Period. The PSUs that become eligible to vest based on performance during the Performance Period shall vest on the Vesting Date set forth in the Grant Notice, subject to Continuous Service through such date, except as expressly provided in Section 2(b), 2(c) or 2(d) below. The Company shall deliver to the Participant on the Settlement Date a number of whole or fractional shares of Common Stock equal to the number of Vested PSUs. The Company may, in its sole discretion, settle any PSUs accrued as dividend equivalents by a cash payment equal to the Fair Market Value of a share of Common Stock on the date of payment (as opposed to payment in the form of shares of Common Stock). “Settlement Date” means: as soon as practicable following the vesting of the PSUs on the Vesting Date but in no event later than December 31 of the calendar year in which the Vesting Date occurs.

(b)Termination without Cause under the Executive Severance Plan. For a Participant who is subject to the terms of the Western Digital Corporation Amended and Restated Executive Severance Plan, as applicable (or any applicable successor plan) (the “Executive Severance Plan”) at the time of termination of Continuous Service, then upon Participant’s termination of employment by the Company without Cause (as defined in the Executive Severance Plan) under circumstances that would entitle the Participant to severance benefits under the Executive Severance Plan, subject to compliance with the terms of the Executive Severance Plan, then the PSUs will be payable in accordance with the Vesting Schedule set forth in the Grant Notice above, with no acceleration, and vest as follows:

would prevent the Participant from otherwise earning a living. The Participant agrees that the Restrictive Covenants do not confer a benefit upon the Company and its Subsidiaries that is disproportionate to the detriment of the Participant.

(d) The Participant agrees that a breach by the Participant of any of the covenants in this Section 13 would cause immediate and irreparable harm to the Company that would be difficult or impossible to measure, and that damages to the Company for any such injury would therefore be an inadequate remedy for any such breach. The Participant further agrees that the applicable period of time any Restrictive Covenant is in effect following the date of the Participant’s termination of Continuous Service shall be extended by the same amount of time that the Participant is in breach of any Restrictive Covenant following the date on which the Participant’s Continuous Service terminates. The Participant further agrees that in the event of any breach of any provision of this Section 13, in addition to and without limitation upon all other remedies the Company (or any of its Subsidiaries) may have under this Award Document, at law or otherwise, this Award (to the extent outstanding at the time of such breach) shall automatically terminate and be forfeited as of the time of such breach.

brief.thesis: Vishay's latest provided primary excerpt supports materially improved liquidity after the 2026 equity raise and much better 2026 year-to-date earnings and operating cash flow versus the prior-year period, but the supplied evidence is too incomplete to validate the capital structure details, current debt maturity profile, revolver status, covenant headroom, receivables-securitization dependence, or a supported valuation. The preliminary research overstates what the excerpt proves and contains factual errors.
brief.decline_reason: Primary evidence is partial and does not support key recovery-underwriting claims about revolver payoff, remaining note balance composition, covenant cushion, refinancing risk, or valuation. Several preliminary figures are incorrect or period-mismatched.
brief.temporary_vs_structural: Evidence for a temporary recovery exists: 2026 Q3 revenue, operating income, and net income improved sharply year over year, and 2026 nine-month operating cash flow improved materially. But structural conclusions are not yet supported because the excerpt does not include the debt footnotes or financing amendment text needed to verify how durable the balance-sheet improvement is.
brief.financial_resilience: As of 2026-10-03, the provided 10-Q excerpt shows cash and cash equivalents of 1139887000, short-term investments of 5304000, total current assets of 2550790000, total current liabilities of 769592000, and stockholders' equity of 2954378000. The same excerpt's cash-flow statement shows 2026 nine-month operating cash flow of 314791000 and capital expenditures of 253409000, implying only modest nine-month cash generation before any further financing needs. Liquidity looks better than at 2025-12-31, but debt composition and contractual maturities are not adequately evidenced in the supplied text.
brief.competition_and_technology: The excerpt supports that Vishay sells a broad portfolio of discrete semiconductors and passive components across industrial, automotive, military/aerospace, healthcare, and other end markets. That breadth can help resilience, but the supplied evidence does not establish pricing power, substitution resistance, or sustained technology leadership relative to competitors.
risks: Preliminary note error: latest-quarter revenue was 978939000, not 74800000.

The 2026-07-01 8-K provided is an equity offering filing, not a financing-amendment text proving updated loan maturities or covenants.

Nine-month operating cash flow benefited from working-capital movements and included 29875000 of stock compensation expense; the excerpt does not provide a clean trailing annual equity-cash measure after financing costs.
Capital expenditures remained high at 253409000 for the first nine fiscal months of 2026, limiting internally generated cash despite stronger operations.
Partial excerpts omit debt footnotes, covenant definitions, restricted-cash detail, securitization terms, and any subsequent amendment that may supersede older financing schedules.
Weighted average basic shares for the 2026 quarter and nine-month period were materially above the prior year, consistent with meaningful dilution from the follow-on offering.

Need contractual maturity tables and covenant terms to assess debt due in months 13-24 and stressed headroom.

brief.catalyst: Potential catalyst exists if later primary filings confirm that equity proceeds permanently reduced higher-risk borrowings while elevated capital spending starts yielding better segment earnings and cash conversion, but that catalyst is not yet fully evidenced in the supplied excerpts.

brief.thesis: Primary-source review supports that Valero remained highly profitable and liquid through 2026-09-30, but the preliminary notes overstated what the filings prove. The strongest current evidence is operational and balance-sheet strength, not a sourced recovery valuation. Because the available primary excerpts do not provide a complete current contractual maturity/covenant package or a retrieved financing amendment, and because the new Houston transaction economics beyond purchase price are still forward-looking, the name stays in follow-up rather than cleared as a supported recovery case.
brief.decline_reason: The retrieved primary filings do not establish why the shares fell about 20% from the recent peak; that price move should not be reverse-engineered from incomplete excerpts.
brief.temporary_vs_structural: Evidence so far points more to cyclical volatility than franchise impairment. The business generated 2026 year-to-date operating income of 16000000000 and net cash provided by operating activities of 13902000000 for the nine months ended 2026-09-30, versus much weaker 2025 comparables, which argues against a currently visible structural collapse. However, refining remains margin-sensitive, and the supplied excerpts are insufficient to clear medium-term regulatory, refinery incident, or project-execution risks.
brief.financial_resilience: Corrections to the preliminary notes: as of 2026-09-30, the company reported cash and cash equivalents of 9840000000; total debt of 8579000000; total finance lease obligations of 2422000000; and total debt plus finance lease obligations of 11001000000. Debt and leases must be separated; they are not the same obligation class. Also, the cited 5298000000 of committed liquidity was from the 2025-12-31 10-K, not the 2026-09-30 10-Q, so it is stale and should not be presented as current-quarter cash or current-quarter committed liquidity. The current portion line of 989000000 is a balance-sheet amount, not a full contractual maturity schedule. The 2026-10-22 earnings release further states that 100000000 of 7.65% debentures due in July and 426000000 of 3.400% senior notes due in September were repaid, so those specific maturities should not be treated as still outstanding after 2026-09-30.
brief.competition_and_technology: The supplied primary evidence still supports scale and diversification: the 2026-10-30 transaction press release describes 14 refineries with about 3.0 million barrels per day of throughput capacity, renewable diesel capacity of about 1.2 billion gallons per year through DGD, and 12 ethanol plants with about 1.7 billion gallons per year. That suggests durable operating scale, but it does not by itself prove pricing power, immunity from substitution, or returns on new capital.
risks: Forward-looking Houston acquisition economics are unproven in the retrieved excerpts; only the 320500000 purchase price, expected closing by end of 2026, and an initial restart expectation of 165000 BPD by year-end 2027 are stated.

No retrieved current financing amendment or full debt footnote package was provided here, so contractual maturities beyond the balance-sheet current portion, covenant headroom, restricted cash, and amendment terms remain unresolved.

Available facility capacity is not cash, and stale 2025 liquidity tables should not be used as current-quarter evidence.
Finance lease obligations are material at 2422000000 and should not be conflated with funded debt when assessing refinancing risk.
The retrieved excerpts do not provide a primary-source valuation framework sufficient to support upside claims.

Valero to Acquire Former Houston Refinery from LyondellBasell
•Plans to Restart 165,000 BPD of Throughput Capacity by Year-End 2027

SAN ANTONIO, October 30, 2026 – Valero Energy Corporation (NYSE: VLO, “Valero”) announced today that its wholly owned subsidiary, Valero Refining-Texas, L.P., entered into a definitive agreement to acquire all the outstanding equity interests of LYB Houston Hub Holdings LLC (“LYB Houston”) from a subsidiary of LyondellBasell Industries N.V. (“Lyondell”) for a purchase price of $320.5 million, subject to closing adjustments. Closing of the transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including the expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, and is expected to occur by the end of 2026. LYB Houston indirectly owns an approximately 700-acre facility adjacent to Valero’s Houston refinery on the Houston Ship Channel in Texas that operated as a petroleum refinery. Valero currently expects to initially restart 165,000 BPD of light sweet crude processing capacity by year-end 2027. The acquisition also provides the opportunity to later invest in high-complexity, heavy sour crude processing.

“This acquisition is a unique opportunity to strategically expand Valero’s U.S. Gulf Coast footprint at a fraction of replacement value and enhance the long-term strength of our refining system,” said Lane Riggs, Chairman, CEO and President of Valero. “It is expected to provide a compelling financial return, consistent with Valero’s disciplined capital allocation framework, while generating attractive commercial optimization opportunities and supporting future investment in high-complexity, heavy sour crude oil processing.”
Valero has prepared a presentation related to the transaction, which will be posted on its Investor Relations website and furnished as an exhibit in a Current Report on Form 8-K.
About Valero

Valero Energy Corporation, through its subsidiaries (collectively, Valero), is a multinational manufacturer and marketer of petroleum-based and low-carbon liquid transportation fuels and petrochemical products, and sells its products primarily in the United States (U.S.), Canada, the United Kingdom (U.K.), Ireland, and Latin America. Valero operates 14 petroleum refineries

located in the U.S., Canada, and the U.K. with a combined throughput capacity of approximately 3.0 million barrels per day. Valero is a joint venture member in Diamond Green Diesel Holdings LLC, which produces low-carbon fuels including renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), with a production capacity of approximately 1.2 billion gallons per year in the U.S. Gulf Coast region. See the annual report on Form 10-K for more information on SAF. Valero also owns 12 ethanol plants located in the U.S. Mid-Continent region with a combined production capacity of approximately 1.7 billion gallons per year. Valero manages its operations through its Refining, Renewable Diesel, and Ethanol segments. Please visit investorvalero.com for more information.

brief.thesis: Primary SEC excerpts support that PDF Solutions entered 2026-09-30 with solid reported liquidity, growing revenue, and positive year-to-date GAAP profitability, but the recovery/valuation case is not yet supported because free-cash durability is unclear after elevated equipment spending, the newer financing agreement exists but its actual terms were not retrieved, and a cited Q3 earnings exhibit was not supplied in readable form.
brief.decline_reason: Shares appear to have fallen from a recent peak, but the primary evidence reviewed does not show that the decline is clearly temporary mispricing rather than a rational response to weak trailing free cash generation and unresolved financing details.
brief.temporary_vs_structural: Evidence for temporary pressure: 2026 nine-month revenue rose to USD 189993000 from USD 156621000, operating income improved to USD 19663000 from USD 2389000, deferred revenue increased to USD 36727000 from USD 20306000, and cash increased to USD 107131000 at 2026-09-30. Evidence for possible structural pressure: recurring revenue mix fell to 86% year-to-date from 92%, upfront revenue mix rose to 14% from 8%, and nine-month property and equipment purchases were USD 39407000 versus operating cash flow of USD 31834000, so reported earnings improvement did not yet convert into self-funding cash generation on the excerpted evidence.
brief.financial_resilience: At 2026-09-30, cash and cash equivalents were USD 107131000, current assets were USD 257185000, and current liabilities were USD 78106000. Gross funded debt was approximately USD 65333000, consisting of current portion of long-term debt USD 2237000 plus long-term debt USD 63096000. Operating lease liabilities were separate at USD 2025000 current and USD 6278000 non-current, so debt and lease obligations should not be conflated. On that basis, the company had net cash of roughly USD 41798000 before considering any off-balance-sheet or unavailable facility details. However, nine-month cash growth was heavily aided by USD 81791000 of net secondary-offering proceeds, while financing cash flow also included debt repayment and debt issuance costs; this weakens any claim that current cash growth was purely operational.
brief.competition_and_technology: The provided excerpts support exposure to semiconductor manufacturing data, analytics, software, services, CV systems, DirectScan systems, and secureWISE-related offerings, with revenue growth in both Platform and Volume-based categories. They do not provide enough primary evidence to conclude durable pricing power, moat stability, or low substitution risk. The business may benefit from customer wins and backlog growth mentioned in the Q2 2026 earnings exhibit, but comparable Q3 exhibit content was not retrieved, so competitive momentum beyond the 10-Q operating results remains only partially evidenced.
risks: Unread financing exhibit from the 2026-04-24 8-K means current maturity, amortization, collateral, covenant, and amendment details are unresolved.
Trailing free cash generation is not supported by the primary excerpts because nine-month operating cash flow of USD 31834000 was below property and equipment purchases of USD 39407000.
Cash build in 2026 was materially supported by equity issuance proceeds of USD 81791000, so per-share recovery quality is weaker than cash balance alone suggests.
Revenue mix became less recurring year-to-date in 2026 versus 2025, which may increase volatility if upfront items normalize.
The excerpts reviewed do not support any strong covenant-headroom claim; absence of covenant trouble language is not clearance.
Customer demand remains tied to semiconductor spending and backlog conversion, while the excerpts do not prove backlog quality or margin durability.
unresolved: The preliminary note's claimed debt maturity schedule extending to 2030 was not verified from the supplied excerpts reviewed here.
The 2026-04-24 8-K confirms a material definitive agreement and direct financial obligation, but Exhibit 10.1 itself was not retrieved, so the latest financing terms remain unverified.
The preliminary note relied on a Q3 2026 earnings-release exhibit URL that was not included among the provided readable primary excerpts; its statements should not be treated as verified here.
The partial excerpts do not provide enough evidence on restricted cash, revolving availability, covenant definitions, pricing grids, or refinancing triggers.
No primary-source valuation support was retrieved for equity cash after all normalization adjustments, so scenario valuation is unavailable.
The excerpts reviewed do not establish a five-year post-split/post-spin comparable price framework or a supported return target.
brief.catalyst: Next hard checkpoint is the next annual filing or financing-related amendment that fully discloses current debt terms, covenant package, amortization, and whether operating cash flow begins to cover investment spend without equity issuance.
brief.invalidation: A weaker stance would be invalidated positively if a subsequent filing shows sustained operating cash flow exceeding equipment investment, limited dilution after the 2026 offering, and verified financing terms with comfortable covenant headroom and no near-term refinancing pressure. It would be invalidated negatively if later filings show continuing sub-FCF operations, more equity financing, or tighter debt terms than currently evidenced.
brief.checkpoint_metric: Verify from the next SEC filing whether trailing operating cash flow exceeds trailing property and equipment purchases, and whether any newer debt amendment changes maturity, amortization, or covenants.
brief.opportunity_cost: Without a verified valuation or clearer self-funded cash conversion, capital may be better reserved for durable software or semiconductor-adjacent names with primary-source-supported FCF and financing visibility.

bear.rationale: No credible primary-source-supported valuation framework was established from the retrieved excerpts. Elevated investment spending, equity issuance in 2026, and unread financing terms prevent a supported bear valuation scenario.

base.rationale: No credible primary-source-supported valuation framework was established from the retrieved excerpts. The evidence is sufficient for operational follow-up, not for assigning a supported base equity cash figure or multiple.

recovery.rationale: No credible primary-source-supported recovery valuation is available because the excerpts do not prove normalized equity cash generation, and the latest financing amendment terms were not read.

sources.finding: Q3 and nine-month 2026 10-Q excerpt supports balance-sheet amounts, income statement improvement, operating cash flow of USD 31834000 for nine months, property and equipment purchases of USD 39407000, separate operating lease liabilities, deferred revenue growth, share-count increase, and revenue-mix shift toward more upfront revenue.

FY2025 10-K excerpt supports 2025 revenue growth, near-breakeven GAAP results, operating cash flow of USD 24053000, material 2025 investing outflows including acquisition and property/equipment spend, and year-end 2025 debt and lease balances.

8-K index confirms a filing on 2026-04-24 under Items 1.01 and 2.03 with an Exhibit 10.1, indicating a material agreement and direct financial obligation, but the actual agreement text was not retrieved, so terms remain unresolved.

Q2 2026 earnings-release exhibit supports second-quarter revenue, margin, backlog, and management commentary, but does not replace the need to read the later Q3 earnings exhibit or financing agreement text.

2011 STOCK INCENTIVE PLAN – Performance STOCK UNIT AGREEMENT

1. Award of Stock Units. PDF Solutions, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the “Company”), has authorized the grant to you of a performance stock unit award (the “Award”) according to the performance stock unit (“PSU”) program set forth in Exhibit A attached hereto and covering the target number of shares of Shares (the “Stock Units”) set forth in the Notice of Performance Stock Unit Award or online Grant Summary (as applicable, the “Notice”) delivered to you along with this 2011 Stock Incentive Plan – Performance Stock Unit Agreement (the “PSU Agreement”), on the date set forth therein (the “Grant Effective Date”), subject to the terms, definitions and provisions of the 2011 Stock Incentive Plan, as amended and restated from time to time (the “Plan”), which is incorporated in this PSU Agreement by reference. Unless otherwise defined in this PSU Agreement or the Notice, the terms used in this PSU Agreement shall have the meanings defined in the Plan.
(a) Bookkeeping Entry. Pursuant to the Plan, each Stock Unit is a bookkeeping entry representing the equivalent in value of one (1) Share.

(b) Acceptance; Cancellation. You acknowledge that by electronically accepting the Award (or instructing the Company in writing to record such acceptance with its designated third-party broker) you agree to be bound by all terms applicable to the Award, as set forth in this PSU Agreement and the Plan. You must expressly accept the terms and conditions of your Stock Units as set forth in the Notice, this PSU Agreement and the Plan by electronically accepting this PSU Agreement within ninety (90) days after the Company first makes the Notice available to you. If you do not accept this Award in the manner instructed by the Company, this Award and all Stock Units represented hereby may be cancelled by the Company in its discretion.

2. Vesting of Stock Units. Subject to the terms and conditions of this PSU Agreement and the Plan, the Stock Units shall vest based on the Participant’s continued Service requirement and the achievement of the market-based performance conditions, as described in the Notice and Exhibit A. So long as your Service continues, the Stock Units shall vest according to the vesting schedule in the Notice and in accordance with the terms set forth in Exhibit A. If you take a leave of absence, the Company may, at its discretion, suspend vesting during the period of leave to the extent permitted under applicable law. Prior to the time that the Stock Units are settled upon vesting, you shall have no rights other than those of a general creditor of the Company. The Stock Units represent an unfunded and unsecured obligation of the Company.

3. Termination of Service. Except as otherwise provided in the Company’s severance plan, change-in-control plan, or an employment or severance agreement approved by the Committee, all unvested Stock Units shall be forfeited upon termination of Service. For purposes of the Stock Units, your Service will be considered terminated as of the date you are no longer actively providing services (regardless of the reason for or the circumstances of such termination) and your right to vest in the Stock Units will terminate effective as of such date and will not be extended by any notice period (e.g., active service would not include any contractual notice period or any period of “garden leave” or similar period mandated under employment laws in the jurisdiction where you are employed or the terms of your employment agreement, if any). The Committee shall have the exclusive discretion to determine when you are no longer actively providing services for purposes of the Stock Units.

4. Settlement of Stock Units. Upon vesting of Stock Units, Stock Units shall be automatically settled in Shares, provided that the Company shall have no obligation to issue Shares pursuant to this PSU Agreement unless and until you have satisfied any applicable tax and/or other obligations pursuant to Section 5 below and such issuance otherwise complies with all applicable law.

text_blocks.text: PDF Solutions® Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Santa Clara, CA, August 6, 2026 – PDF Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: PDFS), a leading provider of comprehensive data solutions for the semiconductor and electronics ecosystem, today announced financial results for its second quarter ended June 30, 2026.
Financial Highlights of Second Quarter 2026

● Quarterly total revenues of $61.5 million, up 19% over last year’s comparable quarter ● GAAP gross margin of 69% and non-GAAP gross margin of 73% ● GAAP operating margin of 8% and non-GAAP operating margin of 22% ● GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.10 and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.27 ● Ending backlog of $270.7 million
text_blocks.preceding_context: Santa Clara, CA, August 6, 2026 – PDF Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: PDFS), a leading provider of comprehensive data solutions for the semiconductor and electronics ecosystem, today announced financial results for its second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Financial Highlights of Second Quarter 2026

text_blocks.text: Total revenues for the second quarter of 2026 were $61.5 million, compared to $60.1 million for the first quarter of 2026 and $51.7 million for the second quarter of 2025.

GAAP gross margin for the second quarter of 2026 was 69%, compared to 72% for the first quarter of 2026 and 71% for the second quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP gross margin for the second quarter of 2026 was 73%, compared to 76% for the first quarter of 2026 and 76% for the second quarter of 2025.

GAAP operating margin for the second quarter of 2026 was 8%, compared to 10% for the first quarter of 2026 and 2% for the second quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP operating margin for the second quarter of 2026 was 22%, compared to 25% for the first quarter of 2026 and 19% for the second quarter of 2025.

GAAP net income for the second quarter of 2026 was $4.3 million, or $0.10 per diluted share, compared to net income of $4.8 million, or $0.12 per diluted share, for the first quarter of 2026, and net income of $1.1 million, or $0.03 per diluted share, for the second quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP net income for the second quarter of 2026 was $11.4 million, or $0.27 per diluted share, compared to non-GAAP net income of $12.6 million, or $0.31 per diluted share, for the first quarter of 2026, and non-GAAP net income of $7.3 million, or $0.19 per diluted share, for the second quarter of 2025.
Ending backlog for the second quarter of 2026 was $270.7 million, compared to $246.4 for the first quarter of 2026 and $232.6 for the second quarter of 2025.
Financial Outlook

“In the second quarter of 2026, PDF Solutions continued on its growth trajectory, enabled by a broad product and services portfolio developed and curated to address the evolving needs of the semiconductor manufacturing industry,” said John Kibarian, CEO and President of the Company. He continued, “In the quarter, we had major customer wins for our secureWISE system, for our DirectScan system, and for our Exensio product and services. We significantly increased backlog in the quarter, which we expect to add to revenue for a number of years. Taking into account these positive factors, we reaffirm our 20% annual revenue growth target for 2026.”

Non-GAAP gross profit and margin exclude stock-based compensation expense and the amortization of acquired technology under costs of revenues. Non-GAAP net income excludes stock-based compensation expense, amortization of acquired intangible assets, amortization of debt issuance costs and the effects of certain non-recurring items, such as expenses for certain legal proceedings, acquisition-related and integration costs, and their related income tax effects, as applicable, as well as adjustments for the valuation allowance for deferred tax assets and reconciling items. Non-GAAP financial measures are used by management internally to measure the Company’s profitability and performance. PDF Solutions’ management believes that these non-GAAP measures provide useful supplemental information to investors regarding the Company’s ongoing operations in light of the fact that none of these categories of expense and income has a current effect on the future uses of cash (with the exception of expenses related to certain legal proceedings and acquisition-related and integration costs) nor do they impact the generation of current or future revenues. These non-GAAP results should not be considered an alternative to, or a substitute for, GAAP financial information, and may differ from similarly titled non-GAAP measures used by other companies. In particular, these non-GAAP financial measures are not a substitute for GAAP measures of income or loss as a measure of performance, or to cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities as a measure of liquidity. brief.thesis: Primary filings support that Xylem remained profitable and cash-generative through 2026-09-30, but the preliminary notes overstate what is verified. The current primary evidence confirms a new undrawn $1,500,000,000 revolver signed on 2026-09-08, confirms the old $1,000,000,000 revolver was terminated, and shows 2026-09-30 balance-sheet debt of $2,895,000,000 split between $530,000,000 current maturities/short-term borrowings and $2,365,000,000 long-term debt. However, the provided excerpts do not give enough complete, current primary evidence on the post-September debt stack, covenant headroom, refinancing path for current maturities, five-year resilience, or valuation support to underwrite a recovery case.
brief.decline_reason: Shares were down about 21% from the 2026-08-14 recent peak in the supplied market snapshot, but the primary excerpts here do not establish whether that decline is temporary dislocation or a justified reset. The Q3 2026 income statement shows revenue down year over year for the quarter ($2,201,000,000 vs. $2,268,000,000) even as profitability improved.
brief.temporary_vs_structural: Evidence cuts both ways. Temporary positives: net income attributable to Xylem rose to $747,000,000 for the first nine months of 2026 from $622,000,000 a year earlier, and operating cash flow for the first nine months was $729,000,000. Structural cautions: Q3 revenue declined year over year, cash fell to $708,000,000 from $1,479,000,000 since year-end, and financing cash outflow was heavily affected by $1,580,000,000 of repurchases and $307,000,000 of dividends. That does not prove distress, but it does mean the drawdown cannot be labeled a simple liquidity misunderstanding from these excerpts alone.
brief.financial_resilience: What is verified: as of 2026-09-30, cash and equivalents were $708,000,000; total current assets were $3,952,000,000; total current liabilities were $2,842,000,000; short-term borrowings and current maturities of long-term debt were $530,000,000; and long-term debt, net, was $2,365,000,000. For the first nine months of 2026, cash paid for interest was $39,000,000 and net cash from operations was $729,000,000. What is not verified from these excerpts: restricted cash, full debt maturity ladder, post-quarter refinancing activity, actual revolver usage at 2026-09-30, or stressed covenant headroom.
brief.competition_and_technology: The provided excerpts do not contain enough primary detail to assess competitive durability, technology substitution risk, customer demand resilience, or pricing power. The revenue mix does show both product and service exposure, plus lease revenue, but that is not enough to conclude moat strength.
risks: Current maturities and short-term borrowings of $530,000,000 remained on the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, so the refinancing path cannot be treated as fully solved.
The new 2026 revolver is a commitment, not cash; the 8-K expressly said no borrowings were outstanding at signing.
Balance-sheet debt should not be conflated with leases or full facility size; the credit agreement separately defines capital lease obligations and revolving commitments.
Quarterly revenue declined year over year in Q3 2026 despite higher earnings, so demand/pricing quality needs more evidence.
Cash declined materially year to date, and financing choices included large buybacks; that weakens a simplistic liquidity narrative.
The excerpts are partial, so absence of adverse language is not clearance on covenants, restrictions, or contingent liabilities.
unresolved: Need current earnings 8-K exhibit or full 2026-10-27 results release to verify any revised guidance, restructuring estimates, divestiture plans, or management liquidity claims mentioned in the preliminary notes.
Need any subsequent financing amendment or post-2026-09-30 debt issuance/redemption filing to confirm whether the $530,000,000 current maturities were repaid, refinanced, or remain outstanding.
Need the full revolving credit agreement covenant section and ratio threshold details, not just the existence of a leverage covenant, to assess headroom.
Need primary evidence for total debt composition separating funded notes/loans from lease obligations and any hedging-related carrying-value effects.
Need five-year primary financial history to judge resilience across cycles; current excerpts cover only 2025-12-31 and 2026 year-to-date balances/results.
No credible primary-source valuation support from the permitted retrieved documents; therefore no supported upside case can be published.
brief.catalyst: Nearest useful catalyst is verification of post-2026-09-30 financing and the next results/filing package that clarifies debt maturities, covenant headroom, and whether earnings improvement can persist despite softer quarterly revenue.
brief.invalidation: A recovery review would be further weakened if later filings show revolver usage rising materially, covenant headroom narrowing, current maturities remaining unresolved, or continued quarterly revenue erosion without offsetting cash conversion.
brief.checkpoint_metric: Verify, from the next primary filing package, the exact funded debt composition and whether the 2026-09-30 current maturities/short-term borrowings of $530,000,000 have been refinanced or repaid without meaningful dilution.
brief.opportunity_cost: Without valuation support and with unresolved financing details, capital may be better reserved for industrial names where primary filings more clearly show the maturity ladder, covenant cushion, and recovery economics.

sources.finding: Q3 2026 revenue was $2,201,000,000 versus $2,268,000,000 in Q3 2025; nine-month net income attributable to Xylem was $747,000,000; cash at 2026-09-30 was $708,000,000; short-term borrowings and current maturities of long-term debt were $530,000,000; long-term debt, net, was $2,365,000,000; and nine-month operating cash flow was $729,000,000 with $268,000,000 of capex, $1,580,000,000 of share repurchases, $307,000,000 of dividends, and $39,000,000 cash interest paid.

On 2026-09-08 Xylem entered a senior unsecured five-year revolving credit facility of up to $1,500,000,000, expandable by up to $500,000,000, and the filing states no borrowings were outstanding under the new facility on signing. The same filing states the prior 2023 $1,000,000,000 revolver was terminated.

The attached credit agreement defines the maturity date as the fifth anniversary of the effective date and defines consolidated total indebtedness and capital lease obligations separately, supporting the need not to conflate facility capacity, funded debt, and lease obligations.

On 2026-05-29 Xylem completed a public offering of $500,000,000 of 5.200% senior notes due 2033 and $500,000,000 of 5.450% senior blue notes due 2036. The filing says proceeds were intended in part to repay or redeem the $500,000,000 3.250% senior notes maturing on 2026-11-01 and for general corporate purposes.

text_blocks.text: August 14, 2026
Andrea van der Berg
[address on file]
Dear Andrea,

It is always a pleasure to have the opportunity to acknowledge the accomplishment and contributions of employees who have had an impact on our business. We are pleased to offer you the position of EVP, Chief Finance Officer, reporting directly to Matthew Pine, Xylem’s President & Chief Executive Officer. This position is based in Charlotte, NC and effective September 1, 2026.

Base Salary: You will be compensated on a bi-weekly basis in the amount of $25,961.54, which is equivalent to $675,000 annually. Annual merit increases are normally scheduled for March of each year and are at the discretion of the Leadership Development and Compensation Committee (LDCC) of Xylem’s Board of Directors. You will be able to participate in the merit increase program beginning in 2027, where any merit increases are typically effective and paid out beginning in March.

Annual Incentive Plan: You will be eligible for participation in the Annual Incentive Plan (AIP) for the Executive Leadership Team beginning in 2026 according to the approved parameters of the plan and provided targets are met and certified by the LDCC. Your new bonus target is 80% of base salary. Approved AIP awards are typically paid in March for performance in the previous calendar year and will be prorated based on your new and previous teams and targets.

Annual Long-Term Incentive Plan: You will continue to be eligible to participate in the Xylem Long-Term Incentive Plan (LTIP) and will have an annual target award of $1,750,000 to be provided as 50% Performance Share Units (PSUs), 25% Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and 25% Stock Options, which will be subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable grant agreements. RSUs and Stock Options vest one-third on the first, second and third anniversary of the grant date. The PSUs vest 100% after three years and are payable based on the Company’s performance against targets set by the LDCC. Subsequent annual grants may vary due to management discretion with regard to individual performance and market competitiveness and are subject to approval by the LDCC. Your next full annual LTIP award will be made effective on or about March 1, 2027.

For 2026, you will receive an additional LTIP award of $787,500 to be provided on/about September 1, 2026. The mix and vesting for the grant will be consistent with the most recent annual grant cycle made in March 2026.
Repatriation: We will provide repatriation benefits to you (and your family) to the Charlotte, NC area as per the terms of the Xylem Global Mobility Long Term Local Plus Program.

Benefit Plans: A complete benefits package will be made available to you and your eligible dependents, which includes immediate enrollment in medical plans and subject to any enrollment waiting periods as defined by certain life insurance coverage plans.

Executive Perquisites: You will be eligible to participate in the Executive Physical (up to $5,000) and Tax Preparation Services (up to $5,000) reimbursement program. You will also be eligible to participate in the Company-sponsored Family Cybersecurity Protection Program, which provides enhanced personal cybersecurity and identity protection services.

Paid Time Off: Xylem offers Flexible Time Off (FTO) to US exempt employees. With FTO, colleagues can take time off when they choose (including vacation, sick and personal time). This means there is no specific amount of time off provided – instead, colleagues manage reasonable time away from work with their leader, ensuring they meet mutually agreed on needs for themselves and the team. At Xylem, we encourage our people to stay well, refreshed, and renewed while managing their work with excellence.

Holidays: Xylem recognizes twelve paid holidays per calendar year for eligible employees. Some of these are floating holidays, which may be assigned and are pro-rated based upon your new position start date.

Andrea, congratulations on your new role. We look forward to your continued contributions to our organization. Please acknowledge your acceptance of our offer by signing one copy of this letter and returning it to my attention as soon as possible. You should also retain a copy for your personal files.
Warm regards,
/s/ Matthew Pine

text_blocks.text: On September 8, 2026, Xylem Inc. (the “Company”), as borrower, entered into a Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility Agreement (the “2026 Credit Agreement”), a senior unsecured revolving credit facility, in an aggregate principal amount of up to $1,500,000,000 (available in U.S. dollars and in Euros), with a syndicate of lenders arranged by Citibank, N.A., BNP Paribas Securities Corp., ING Bank N.V., Dublin Branch, JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., Wells Fargo Securities, LLC, as Lead Arrangers and Joint Bookrunners, and with Citibank, N.A., as Administrative Agent, JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as Syndication Agent, ING Capital LLC, as Sustainability Structuring Agent, and BNP Paribas and Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as Documentation Agents. The 2026 Credit Agreement provides for increases of up to $500,000,000 for a maximum aggregate principal amount of $2,000,000,000 at the request of the Company and with the consent of the institutions providing such increased commitments. The facility made available by the 2026 Credit Agreement will be used for working capital and other general corporate purposes.

Interest on all loans under the 2026 Credit Agreement is payable either quarterly or at the expiration of any Term SOFR or EURIBOR interest period applicable thereto. Borrowings accrue interest at a rate equal to, at the Company's election, a base rate or a Term SOFR or EURIBOR rate plus an applicable margin. The 2026 Credit Agreement includes a pricing grid that determines the applicable margin based on the Company's credit rating, with a further adjustment depending on the Company's annual Sustainability Spread Adjustment. The Company will also pay quarterly fees to each lender for such lender's commitment to lend accruing on such commitment at a rate based on the credit rating of the Company, whether such commitment is used or unused, as well as a quarterly letter of credit fee accruing on the letter of credit exposure of such lender during the preceding quarter at a rate based on the credit rating of the Company (as adjusted for the Sustainability Fee Adjustment).
The 2026 Credit Agreement requires the Company to maintain a consolidated total debt to consolidated EBITDA ratio, which will be based on the last four fiscal quarters.

The 2026 Credit Agreement also contains a number of customary covenants, including limitations on the incurrence of secured debt and debt of subsidiaries, liens, sale and lease-back transactions, mergers, consolidations, liquidations, dissolutions and sales of assets. The 2026 Credit Agreement also contains customary events of default.
The Company has the ability to designate subsidiaries that can borrow under the 2026 Credit Agreement, subject to certain requirements and conditions set forth in the 2026 Credit Agreement.
No borrowings are outstanding under the 2026 Credit Agreement on the date hereof.

In connection with entering into the 2026 Credit Agreement, on September 8, 2026 the Company terminated the Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility Agreement, dated March 1, 2023 (the “2023 Credit Agreement”), among the Company, certain lenders and Citibank, N.A. as Administrative Agent, which provided for a senior unsecured $1,000,000,000 revolving credit facility. The 2023 Credit Agreement provided for increases of up to $300,000,000 for a maximum aggregate principal amount of $1,300,000,000 at the request of the Company and with the consent of the institutions providing such increased commitments.

On May 29, 2026, Xylem Inc. (the “Company”) completed a public offering (the “Offering”) of $500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.200% Senior Notes due 2033 (the “2033 Notes”) and $500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.450% Senior Blue Notes due 2036 (the “2036 Blue Notes” and, together with the 2033 Notes, the “Notes”). The Notes are governed by a senior indenture, dated March 11, 2016 (the “Base Indenture”), as supplemented by the first supplemental indenture, dated March 11, 2016 (the “First Supplemental Indenture”), and as further supplemented by the fifth supplemental indenture, dated May 29, 2026 (the “Fifth Supplemental Indenture”), each between Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas, as trustee, and the Company (as so supplemented, the “Indenture”).

The Notes are senior unsecured obligations of the Company and rank equally in right of payment with all of the Company’s other unsecured and unsubordinated obligations from time to time outstanding. The 2033 Notes will bear interest at the rate of 5.200% per year and will mature on June 1, 2033. The 2036 Blue Notes will bear interest at the rate of 5.450% per year and will mature on June 1, 2036. Interest on the Notes will be payable semiannually on June 1 and December 1 of each year beginning on December 1, 2026.

The Company may redeem the Notes at any time, at its option, subject to certain conditions, at specified redemption prices, plus accrued and unpaid interest to the redemption date. The Indenture contains customary agreements and covenants by the Company.
